verdicts.reason: The official API reference shows Bearer authentication using a user-generated API token.

verdicts.quote: "Coda has a public API available to all users."
verdicts.reason: This indicates self-serve access for all users (free and paid) without partner gating or sales.

verdicts.quote: "The Coda REST API allows users to programmatically interact with Coda docs in a number of ways, including:" … "Inserting and updating rows" … "Publishing a doc."
verdicts.reason: The help article enumerates many capabilities across docs, tables/rows, pages, and publishing—consistent with a broad API.
Coda documents and hosts its own MCP server, confirming an official MCP.

verdicts.quote: "On all plan types, docs larger than 125 MB* may not be able to access the Coda API."
verdicts.reason: The API is buildable with self-serve tokens and docs, but caveats include doc-size API lockouts, rate limits, and some write actions requiring Doc Maker role. ([help.coda.io](https://help.coda.io/hc/en-us/articles/39555760015757-Overview-Doc-limits?utm_source=openai))
